Hasbro Bop It Bounce This is the modern version of a game in which you get an electronic paddle, a ball and you can bounce, and it counts the number of bounces and you get an announcer to say it. My nephew enjoyed playing with this little gadget. The voice command cues you through six different games: 1. MAX BOUNCE - You have 30 seconds to bounce the ball and seeing how many times you can bounce it. 2. INFINITY BOUNCE - Just keep on bouncing. 3. HANG TIME - Catch as many air as you can in 5 bounces. 4. RIGHT HEIGHT - The game calls the shots, whether to hit the ball high or low. 5. LITTLE-MIDDLE-BIG - Hit it high, middle or low. 6. FREE FORM - Freestyle bouncing.

I recommend playing outside the house and it is fascinating for young and old. Sometimes when I am tired of reading or watching TV, I play this for few minutes to take my mind off. It is a lot of fun.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Bop It Bounce

QMAN Girls Building Blocks Toys Trendy Cosmetics Store Building Kit Girls Make-Up Shop Street-View Bricks Toy for Girls Age 6-12 and Up (348 Pieces) I tried three of these off-brand LEGO sets in the "street store" model series - the coffee house, the make-up store, and the hair salon. Each of the finished stores is too small for your minifigs to actually use, which is quite disappointing - this is a look-at model only - but also like those models, the final product is quite a winner. Smooth bricks cover every surface, so it doesn't even look like a LEGO set when finished.

The instructions are fine, but certainly not as clear as they would be if made by LEGO, who have a long history of writing the best manuals in the business. These will do, but are certainly not entirely clear.

The tilted coffee cup on the roof of the cafe really makes this one stand out, and it offers a lot of interesting pieces that make this one stand out. This is the clear winner of the three I tried, and if I only bought one, this would be it.

The make-up store and the hair salon were both good, but looked a lot more typical when finished. They are quite colorful, and have some unique aspects in the interior. These sets were fine, but slightly more difficult to build, and a little bit more finicky in terms of detail work. The final product is a lot less identifiable, but they still look good on the shelf, and have plenty in them that you can use in other models.
text_fidelity_b: QMAN Girls Building Blocks Toys Trendy Cosmetics Store Building Kit Girls Make-Up Shop Street-View Bricks Toy for Girls Age 6-12 and Up (348 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a: KidKraft Deluxe Wooden Fire Rescue Play Set with Ambulance, Fire Truck, Helicopter, Firefighters, 27 Pieces, Gift for Ages 3+ The toy is well-designed and promises many hours of creative play for my fire-fighter enthusiast grandson. It was easy to put together, with excellent instructions. The construction seems sturdy. I didn't give it five stars because of several factors. I deducted one star for poor paint quality. There were scratches in the paint finish, and the worst were on the header with "Fire Station" painted on it, just where it will be the most visible. The paint seems very thin, and flaked areas look like they'll easily spread with use. In many places, the paint came off when I peeled the part-number stickers off. I deducted the second star because the accessories were not as advertised in the listing or the video. Missing were the doghouse; one of the basketball standards (two were shown; only one was included); the bathroom sink; and one firefighter (two were included; the description promises three). The firefighter's helmet makes it nearly impossible for him to fit through the holes to slide down the pole. The Dalmatian dog pictured was replaced by a brown dog, with a dog bed that he does not fit into, instead of the doghouse. The TV/bookcase console was replaced by a freestanding TV on a pole that is very unrealistic looking. The included accessories match the parts-list in the instruction booklet, so I know the omissions were not accidental.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Deluxe Wooden Fire Rescue Play Set with Ambulance, Fire Truck, Helicopter, Firefighters, 27 Pieces, Gift for Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Dream House Arrived yesterday in a big box. Parts loosely tossed inside, some in plastic bags. The included instructions are so BAD that we didn't/couldn't even use them to assemble the Dream House. We relied mainly on the pictures on the front of the box to guide us.

Pieces are initially hard to snap together. Some of the white columns go in very specific places so I had to take some out and replace them with others. Luckily, I had 2 kids and another adult helping me assemble this thing. The main elevator gets stuck at the second level and I need to work on that some more to get it functioning properly, if possible. The plastic parts are durable enough, I still felt I had to be extra careful to avoid breaking any of them. After we had it mostly assembled I was able to finally snap all the columns in place whereas before no matter how hard I tried I couldn't get them to snap firmly into the bases.

A LOT of accessories are included from silverware to bathroom fixtures, jewelry, etc...so there are LOT of small parts to suck up in the vacuum cleaner or for a pet (like ours) to chew up. We will have to be extra careful about those but they are nice to have to complete the Dream House environment. A sticker page is included that you peel and stick to various areas of the house to make it seem more realistic - fireplace, etc...

Although I had a hard time assembling it (don't try to assemble it on an empty stomach), I didn't for once lose my cool and toss it out the window. We got it assembled, it looks pretty cool to be honest. And my 9 year old daughter absolutely went nuts over it. She loves Barbie and this Dream House is like a parallel Universe to her which she can escape into make-believe land instead of watching TV. Even her tomboy sister likes to play with it. I don't know if it will maintain it's appeal after a while, but despite it's difficulty in assembly, and the horrible instructions (just small black and white pictures, no words whatsoever), you can assemble it if you are patient and keep trying different parts and studying the pictures on the box.

And it's pretty tall....at least 4 feet high. The barbie dolls fit nicely inside of it and overall it's a pretty cool thing to look at when it's completely assembled and all the furniture and stuff is placed inside it. I would have loved to have had one of these when I was a kid. Is it worth $159.00? I don't know. I might would have paid at least a hundred for it.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dream House

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll Since the first Barbie doll was created in 1959, little girl's have always loved to style/color Barbie doll's hair, and this fun to color hair Barbie is no exception. (I took my 1960's ponytail down, so she could look like Sleeping Beauty back in the day!) This gorgeous Color Stylin' Hair Barbie is a huge favorite with the grandchildren now.

Barbie comes with a suction cupped chair, comb, applicator brush, bowl, seven color swatches in 3 colors-3 pink, 2 purple and 2 orange, clip on foiler holder and rubberbands. Barbie is dressed in a glittery pink dress with shoes, necklace and belt. The color application is easy- seat Barbie in her chair, which doesn't move due to an ingenious suction cup bottom, wet the hair section you want to color, place the color swatch in the foiler, then clip the foiler to the wet hair and pull through. When you want to remove the color or color again, you just wash and dry the hair and you are ready for more fun.

There are a couple things you should know before using this coloring set: don't color near carpet, furniture, walls or clothes you don't want to ruin, as these colors can be a permanent stain for certain fabrics or walls. I laid down a cheap plastic tablecloth from the dollar store, so the girls had a great area to play on with no worries. I called Mattel, and found they do not sell extra color swatches, so once these are used up, they are gone, and to replace the colors, you would have to buy another doll. This is a shame, as they always sell accessories and extra hair swatches for the dolls with hair swatches that can be cut, so why not some inexpensive color swatches too Mattel?

The girls just love coloring, braiding and styling the gorgeous streaked areas of this Barbie's hair, so of course they want more colors- and even different colors too. As for something interesting I noticed, I bought another one of these dolls, as I have 2 granddaughters, and we immediately noticed one set colored darkly and another set colored very faintly. I looked closely at the boxes and what did I find on the backs of the boxes, but an expiration date! It says Best Used By and then a date which you need a magnifying glass to read. Reading the back of our boxes showed that one of the boxes colors was expired! That explains the faint color! Being a wonderfully fun to play with Barbie gives this doll 5 Stars, but color that is expired and having no refills brings her down to limited playability with the color, making this gorgeous Barbie a 4 Star doll.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll

Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game Onitama is a 2-player only game that tries to have a theme, but is really quite abstract.

When I heard about it, I was really quite intrigued that this would be added to the Dice Tower Essentials line as an abstract; after all, isn't Tom Vasel the guy who dislikes most abstracts because they're not theme-y enough? Yet here is the third game in his very quality game series that is otherwise highly thematic, and he goes with an abstract. Seemed like the game must be incredible to have cracked that list as an abstract.

I played a number of times with my wife, who admittedly likes this game quite a lot more than I do. I find the game similar to chess or the Duke, in which you have a certain number of moves, represented by cards, and you move your pieces around the board, switching cards with your opponent along the way. There is a lot of doublethink - If I do this, then they know I'll do that next turn, so they might do this... - and I like that element of the game, but the limitation on my moves did tend to cramp my style a little more, and I'd find myself wishing I just had more options. That skill can probably be built up over time playing with this one, but I don't know if it grabbed me enough to make me invest my time with it.

If 3.5 were an option, I'd go with that. Just not my style, and not as good as the expectations led me to believe.
text_fidelity_b: Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game

Learning Resources Botley The Coding Robot - 45 Pieces, Ages 5+ Screen- Free Coding Toys, Coding STEM Toy for Kids, Coding for Kids,Back to School Gifts,Teacher Supplies Botley is quite a versatile fellow.

My four year old is having fun running him around in "line" mode, where his sensors follow a black lined path on a white background. When he reaches the end, he turns around and comes back.

Daddy is having a little more fun with "code" mode, which is too complex for the little one at this point. You program multiple commands into the remote, and then you send Botley out on a small adventure, around the obstacle course pieces that you can set up with material from the box. It's simple and easy for an adult, but for kids, it will teach computer programming basics, planning ahead, and thinking before you act.

The box comes with a variety of cones, bricks and blocks, as well as arms for Botley and cards that can help you measure how far he's going to move, and doubles as a wavy black line pattern on the reverse side if you want to use it. All told, it's a fun and complete package, although I wish the instructions were a little more explicit for adults, and a little more fun for little ones to explore on their own. As it stands, the manual explains a few little tasks you can try, written in tiny font in as few pages as humanly possible. I want more from this.
text_fidelity_b: Learning Resources Botley The Coding Robot - 45 Pieces, Ages 5+ Screen- Free Coding Toys, Coding STEM Toy for Kids, Coding for Kids,Back to School Gifts,Teacher Supplies

-The value of the craft items for the cost of the set is probably only worth it for big crafters. Consider getting TWO so that the kids can have more fun. Heck... get four! The mess can be rinsed off easy with a garden hose. Oh, Google Bubble Soap Mix. You will be surprised how much fun this can be when you have an endless supply of Bubble mix!

text_fidelity_a:
Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model I bought this model for my 7 year old grandson who recently started riding and currently aspires to be a Vet. The model is small and some of the bits are tiny but manageable if one has reasonable dexterity. It is not for the easily frustrated as it requires patience and a thought to put together. The documentation is marginally helpful, and we used the picture on the cover more that we did the provided sheet for guidance. I also bought "Horse Anatomy (Dover Nature Coloring Book)" which proved a useful addition.
I worked with my grandson to put the model together for the first time. One of the small pieces had molding flash still attached which prevented it from fitting properly until the excess material was removed. The pieces will all fit together properly, but the final assembly is not terribly robust.
To reiterate, it was a bit of a problem solving exercise to fit the pieces into the correct spots, but we found the feeling of accomplishment worth the effort. I do not recommend this as a quick-assembly toy. There are better choices for that purpose. However, I do recommend it as a learning exercise for the curious child. It was fun to see my grandson made associations with his dog and human anatomy during the process. The finished product is suitable for display in a safe spot and can be disassembled and reassembled as long as one keeps track of all the pieces (you wouldn't want to lose his pancreas, would you?). I deducted a star for the less than great documentation.
text_fidelity_b: Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model

text_fidelity_a:
Classic Yahtzee, An Exciting Game Of Skill And Chance for age 8 and up In the 50's and 60's Board Games and Cards were very popular. I remember playing Yahtzee in the 60's mainly with older family than with friends. The older people in the 50's and 60's loved cards- my Mother's friends had Bridge Clubs and the men loved their Poker Nights. I always felt Yahtzee was a combination of a board type game using dice combined with the skill of cards.

The object of Yahtzee is to get the most points by figuring out the points the dice will give you with 3 of a kind, large straight, full house, aces and other card type combinations. You get three chances to roll the most points you can figure out. You really had to figure out which dice would get you more points on the upper section or the lower section of your score card to score high. They even included chips in the game, as you could get a chip for every 100 points you score.

When you roll the 5 dice all the same number, that was Yahtzee. It's nice to see Classic games coming around again to enjoy. For anyone who likes the strategy of playing cards, only with rolling 5 dice, Yahtzee brings that and more to this classic 50's game of both skill and chance.
text_fidelity_b: Classic Yahtzee, An Exciting Game Of Skill And Chance for age 8 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch I'm going to review this not from the perspective of a toy, but rather as a piece of movie memorabilia. Years ago, I use to love to go to the local mall here in Austin and stop by the SunCoast Motion Picture Company store. Where you could buy all sort of movie related items as well as the movies themselves. Over the years I've bought a number of items very similar to this Rocket Raccoon figure for my collection. So when I was offered one of these 10 inch figure to check out I gladly accepted.

I wasn't expecting this figure to be so big - I knew it was suppose to be 10" but it seems bigger than that to me. It came in one of those open face boxes that allow you to actually touch the toy before taking it out of the box, and you can activate the sound effect as the item ships with the batteries already installed and the sound box is set in a demo mode. The sounds it make are pretty loud, they should put a smile on any child face (and a frown on any adults in the room).

Once out of the box, there is some assembly required. You have to pop the tail into the figures rear-end (yeah, I know). It takes some effort to do that, so I suggest having an adult do it. Other than that, the figure is ready to go. Like I mentioned there is a demo mode on the effects box. The effects are controlled with a three-position switch - Off, Try Me (demo), and On. The unit is powered by three double-A batteries which are located in the figures backpack (there is a screw securing the cover to the batteries). Once you turn on the power switch, there are two activation points - one on the figures leg and another on top of the gun he is holding. Pressing one or the other activates both motion and sound effects, plus the figure speaks phrases from the movie. The motion effects are just the end of the gun rotating and the figure shaking a bit. There are some light effects with the end of the gun & gun sight lighting up. There aren't that many spoken phrases - so they can get a bit repetitive after awhile.

The toy is pretty well made - a lot more substantial than most of the movie memorabilia, but then again it was made for kids to play with.

I kept the figure on my desk at work for about a week before bringing it home. I can't tell you how times people stopped and played with the figure (too many times, as that is what prompted me to finally take it home). I haven't seen the movie yet - but it is definitely one that I plan on seeing this summer.

I really like this figure - about the only thing I could comment on would be the detail of the end of his gun, everything else has a decent level of detail, but that part of the gun doesn't. Guessing that is more due to the fact that they made it out of clear plastic so that the light effect could be seen.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch

I would say this one is right down the middle. It's a very straightforward concept - on each card is two choices and you're supposed to pick each one. The problem is that maybe half of them are real dilemmas, while the other half are no brainers. For instance - "would you rather live on a 50th floor penthouse with no elevator or have $2 million in dimes". These are the kinds of questions that might as well not be there because everyone just picks one of the answers and there's no discussion needed, which defeats the point of the game. In some ways I feel like they knew this going in - on the side of the box, it's actually printed that the playtime is up to 60 minutes - with 200 cards, that averages out to 3 cards per minute.

All in all, can't really recommend. You could probably spend an afternoon and come up with better ideas on your own.

text_fidelity_a:
Asmodee Hit Z Road This is a very silly game, despite the theme. Not a gory or cartoonish zombie game, it really could be almost anything in place of them: Mad Max-style marauders, for instance. What's nice about that is, if you're anything like me, and you're totally over all types of zombie games, you will still be able to play Hit Z Road.

This game is really a push your luck dice rolling game with auctions. You're trying to survive until the end of the road, and you need to make some meaningful choices along the way that could make your journey much easier, or much more daring. There is some player elimination, but it's not one of those "you can die on the first turn" types of eliminations - our earliest death was about 10 minutes before the end of the game.

I think a lot of people will find the artwork on this game to be fantastic, and I have to admit that it is daring, different, and one of the most unique looking games out there. While I can admire the work that went into it, the art just doesn't appeal to me.

The name, by the way, might be one of the worst in the history of board gaming.
text_fidelity_b: Asmodee Hit Z Road
